title: Bagpipes
novel:
A new neighbor moved in upstairs, and every night he played the [[bagpipes|bagpipes]]. The sound was [[dreadful|dreadful]] — a long, dying wail that [[pierced|pierce]] the walls.

Marshall and Lily, meanwhile, tried to [[settle|settle]] a quarrel of their own. Marshall had given Barney [[advice|advice]] about Robin, and it had [[backfired|backfire]] badly. Now Barney and Robin were fighting over everything.

"You should [[mind|mind]] your own business," Lily scolded.

But Marshall could not help himself. He liked feeling [[wise|wise]], even when his wisdom [[ruined|ruin]] things.

Barney finally [[confronted|confront]] the bagpipe player upstairs. "Do you know what time it is?" he shouted.

The man kept playing. Barney returned, [[defeated|defeated]].

Ted watched it all and laughed. Some sounds, he thought, could not be silenced — not the [[bagpipes|bagpipes]], and not the [[nagging|nagging]] voice of a friend who thought he knew best. The only [[remedy|remedy]], Ted decided, was patience, and a very good pair of [[earplugs|earplug]].

bagpipes.en: a Scottish musical instrument played by blowing air into a bag

pierce.en: to go through something, especially a sound

advice.en: an opinion about what someone should do

backfire.en: to have the opposite result to what you wanted

mind.en: to care about or pay attention to something

confront.en: to face someone and argue with them

remedy.en: a way of fixing a problem

earplug.en: a small piece you put in your ear to block noise
